messages:
alex: quick follow-up to the offload rfc — proposal for a 'RETIRE' lifecycle state we can use when rebalancing pinned pages. goal: avoid hard-tearing and wasted retries during migrations.

maya: tl;dr? how does RETIRE differ from soft-demote/evictable markers we already use? :thinking: 

alex: short: soft-demote just lowers prefetch/evict priority. RETIRE is explicit: it forbids new pins, hands out an epoch token to in-flight pins, and exposes a cheap E_RETIRED reason to callers. owner drains, migrator moves once epoch is quiescent or TTL expires.

ron: so it's basically a retire-lease. who issues the epoch and who enforces it?

alex: runtime issues an epoch_id on retire(page). page header gets state=RETIRE(epoch_id), new pin attempts return E_RETIRED + hint. existing pins keep their epoch_id and are allowed until they unpin or TTL. after all active pins = 0 or TTL hit, migrator proceeds.

sorin: TTL is importantwe can't allow tenants to hold things forever. proposal: default TTL = 30s, per-tenant override. after TTL, do forced copy-on-write migration and increment page.version to signal staleness.

maya: add telemetry for retire_duration, forced_migrate_count, retire_retries_by_path. ops wants dashboards. also on forced-migrate, capture simple stack-ish sampling to find long-pinners.

liz: interaction with kvcache: we can't let kvcache references point to old backing while migrator moves it. what are the invariants?

alex: plan: page header contains version and epoch. kvcache pins record the header.version they observed. on lookup, if header.version != recorded -> kvcache should retry lookup. migrator after copying new backing bump header.version and install mapping. that makes stale pins detect and retry.

ron: that requires callers to check for E_RETIRED/E_STALE and retry. we have that pattern in some hot paths but not everywhere. adoption work needed.

maya: provide a helper: pin_with_backoff(page, attempts=3, base_ms=10) that handles E_RETIRED/E_STALE with jittered backoff. retrofit hot paths first.

alex: yes. helper + small runtime shim so callers don't explode. also add an opt-in sync_migrate_on_pin_fail flag for critical SLO paths: runtime will block up to S_sync (e.g., 200ms) to finish migration synchronously if configured.

sorin: perf hit of extra header checks? keep header layout small and 64-bit aligned; version & epoch fit in one 64-bit word to keep atomic loads cheap. benchmark that.

liz: rollout plan: 1) internal runtime impl for RETIRE (no consumer changes). 2) land pin_with_backoff helper and migrate a canary service. 3) add kvcache retry paths. 4) enable heartbeat metrics. default TTL 30s, per-tenant knob.

maya: testing matrix: unit tests for header bump, kvcache stale-retry; chaos tests with a sleeping pin > TTL to force forced_migrate; perf microbench for hot-path checks.

ron: also test prefetch: prefetch should consult is_retired(page) and skip prefetch if true; otherwise we waste work. add is_retired inline fast path.

alex: agreed. API examples to include in RFC note:

```
// fast path for callers
ret = page.pin();
if (ret == E_RETIRED || ret == E_STALE) {
  // helper does backoff + retry
  ret = pin_with_backoff(page, 5);
}
```

maya: ops playbook: show when forced_migrate spikes, how to increase TTL per-tenant, and how to roll back retire mode. also add alert on forced_migrate_rate > X/min. i'll own dashboards.

sorin: edge-case: what if migrator dies mid-migrate? need idempotent install: migrator writes new backing, bumps version, then marks old mapping retired. if migrator crashes, a followup migrator can detect partial state by tombstone flag. small state machine required.

liz: add safety: migrator uses two-phase commit to mappings: write new backing, atomically swap mapping pointer with version bump, then free old when GC sees no pins. ensure failure cases are replay-safe.

alex: good. rollout can be opt-in per-cluster. deploy-bot schedule?

deploy-bot: canary runtime build retire-mode=opt-in -> scheduled 2026-03-25T09:00:00Z, canary window 48h.

alex: thanks. i'll draft RFC update with sequence diagram, state machine, and the small helper API. will include expected metrics and dashboards. lgtm? :thumbsup:

maya: lgtm, will run perf microbench and chaos tests in canary.

ron: i'll author unit tests and a small refactor to centralize pin callers.

liz: i'll write ops playbook and tenant config docs.

alex: will post RFC link + branch shortly.

// end thread
